documents.title: For Students (AI guidance)
documents.summary: Student-facing page saying that faculty set AI rules through syllabus statements and that unspecified use is to be treated as forbidden. Unauthorized use may be an Honor Code violation, and students are responsible for accuracy of what they submit.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Some of your faculty may invite you to use generative AI tools ... and some faculty may restrict their use entirely' and that syllabus statements decide, so the rule is left to instructors; the silent-syllabus fallback ('assume that it is forbidden') is a default but does not itself set a course rule.

units.why: States that students 'have access to several generative AI tools with your Middlebury credentials'; the university supplies licensed tools, so P17 (sanctioned tool), informs, general, addressed to students.
units.anchor: you have access to several generative AI tools with your Middlebury credentials

units.why: Access 'places an enormous responsibility on you to consider the potential benefits and harms to yourself as a learner' and society; an ethics/harms framing (P53) rather than accountability for submitted work (P29), so informs.
units.anchor: places an enormous responsibility on you to consider the potential benefits and harms

units.why: 'Some of your faculty may invite you to use generative AI tools ... and some faculty may restrict their use entirely' leaves the permission to each instructor, so P04, informs.
units.anchor: Some of your faculty may invite you to use generative AI tools in your classes

units.why: 'Your faculty should include a syllabus statement indicating what is allowed and what is not allowed' is a recommendation that instructors state AI expectations in the syllabus (P09); actor is instructor, should.
units.anchor: faculty should include a syllabus statement indicating what is allowed and what is not allowed

units.why: 'failure to comply with class policies prohibiting generative AI use could be construed as an Honor Code violation' classes unauthorized AI use as an integrity matter (P36); informs because 'could'.
units.anchor: could be construed as an Honor Code violation, which could result in disciplinary action

units.why: 'you should assume that it is forbidden unless the professor grants you permission verbally or in writing' is the fallback when a syllabus is silent (P06); it binds students and is a restrictive default.
units.anchor: you should assume that it is forbidden unless the professor grants you permission
units.frag_start: If a professor has not specified

units.why: 'You are responsible for the accuracy and integrity of any work you submit, including any work that was created with support of an AI tool' makes students own submitted work (P29), must.
units.anchor: You are responsible for the accuracy and integrity of any work you submit

units.why: 'Middlebury is committed to helping our students engage critically with generative AI tools' is an institution-level statement of purpose and principle (P56), informs.
units.anchor: Middlebury is committed to helping our students engage critically with generative AI tools

units.why: 'We encourage you to participate in events and other learning opportunities that will deepen your understanding' recommends students attend AI learning events; no type covers student AI-literacy events (P63 is faculty only), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: We encourage you to participate in events and other learning opportunities
units.uncovered_note: Institution encourages students to attend events and learning opportunities to deepen AI understanding (student AI literacy support)

documents.title: For Faculty (AI guidance)
documents.summary: Faculty guidance saying instructors choose their own approach and offering three sample syllabus statements (prohibited, limited, supported). It also advises that AI detectors be used only as supplementary evidence.
documents.stance_why: 'Middlebury faculty are empowered to choose their approach' and the page supplies three syllabus statements ranging from forbidden to expected, so the document sets no single stance and lists tiers.

units.why: 'Middlebury faculty are empowered to choose their approach to teaching with generative AI' delegates the decision to instructors (P04).
units.anchor: Middlebury faculty are empowered to choose their approach to teaching with generative AI.

units.why: 'Faculty are asked to provide guidance to students via the course syllabus and to discuss their expectations in class' asks instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus (P09); 'asked' read as should.
units.anchor: Faculty are asked to provide guidance to students via the course syllabus

units.why: 'Middlebury has provided three syllabus statements' (prohibited, limited, allowed or supported) are named levels of AI use, so P05, informs.
units.anchor: Middlebury has provided three syllabus statements that instructors can use or adapt

units.why: 'We recommend starting with this language and adding more specific information for your class' recommends adapting the template into the syllabus; syllabus-statement communication (P09), not tiers (P05).
units.anchor: We recommend starting with this language and adding more specific information for your class.

units.why: 'for each assignment, you can provide guidance on appropriate and inappropriate uses' lets rules be set per assignment, so P04, may.
units.anchor: for each assignment, you can provide guidance on appropriate and inappropriate uses of generative AI

units.why: Sample Option 1: 'Using AI tools ... is forbidden in this class', a ban on AI for the course; default prohibition (P01), addressed to students, must-not.
units.anchor: AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Bard) is forbidden in this class.

units.why: 'You may not use them to assist in any part of your homework or other assignments' bans AI assistance on all submitted work; P19 fits assistance in 'any part', while P01 already holds the course-wide ban.
units.anchor: may not use them to assist in any part of your homework or other assignments.

units.why: 'Any use of generative AI tools will be treated as a violation of Middlebury's Honor Code' makes prohibited use misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: use of generative AI tools will be treated as a violation of Middlebury's Honor Code.

units.why: Option 2: 'You may use AI tools ... to help generate ideas and brainstorm' permits brainstorming (P15), may, limited use.
units.anchor: may use AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Bard) to help generate ideas

units.why: 'only on assignments for which I have given permission to use AI tools, as specified on the syllabus' makes permission assignment-specific (P04); must restricts to permitted assignments.
units.anchor: only on assignments for which I have given permission to use AI tools

units.why: 'Outputs generated by these programs may be inaccurate, incomplete, or otherwise problematic' warns that AI output is unreliable (P31), informs.
units.anchor: Outputs generated by these programs may be inaccurate, incomplete, or otherwise problematic.

units.why: 'I will hold you accountable for the accuracy of your work' makes students answerable for what they submit (P29), must.
units.anchor: I will hold you accountable for the accuracy of your work.

units.why: 'use of AI may also limit your own independent thinking and creativity' gives a learning rationale (P41), informs.
units.anchor: use of AI may also limit your own independent thinking and creativity
units.frag_start: Be aware that use of AI

units.why: 'Do not submit any work generated by an AI tool as your own' bans passing off AI output (P19), must-not.
units.anchor: Do not submit any work generated by an AI tool as your own.

units.why: 'If you include material generated by an AI tool, it should be cited like any other reference material' requires AI citation (P24); P25 not chosen since no tool or prompt details are demanded.
units.anchor: it should be cited like any other reference material

units.why: 'Any un-cited or inappropriate use of AI tools will be treated as a violation of Middlebury's Honor Code' makes missing citation itself the violation (P28), informs.
units.anchor: un-cited or inappropriate use of AI tools will be treated

units.why: Option 3: 'You are expected to use AI tools ... in this class' makes AI use expected, i.e. encouraged by default (P02).
units.anchor: expected to use AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT and image generation tools)

units.why: 'some assignments will require it, with appropriate citation' builds AI into assignments with citation; chosen P24 for the citation duty as P02 already holds the expectation.
units.anchor: some assignments will require it, with appropriate citation
units.frag_start: In fact, some assignments will require it

units.why: 'Learning to use AI is an emerging skill and we will be learning that skill together' justifies AI use as a skill to be taught (P44), informs.
units.anchor: Learning to use AI is an emerging skill and we will be learning that skill

units.why: 'If you have concerns about using these tools, please talk to me ... so that we can find suitable alternatives' offers alternatives when students object to AI, equitable access (P51).
units.anchor: please talk to me about your concerns so that we can find suitable alternatives
units.frag_start: If you have concerns about using

units.why: 'Content detectors such as Turnitin, Pangram, and GPTZero look for repetitive phrasing' describes similarity/AI-detection tools used to identify AI content (P40), informs only.
units.anchor: Content detectors such as Turnitin, Pangram, and GPTZero look for repetitive phrasing

units.why: Middlebury 'needs pedagogical practices that are resilient to technological disruption because they center what AI cannot replicate' says teaching should be redesigned around AI (P35), informs.
units.anchor: pedagogical practices that are resilient to technological disruption because they center what AI cannot replicate

units.why: 'Middlebury is investing in faculty to support the development of new teaching practices' is institutional support for faculty adapting to AI (P63).
units.anchor: Middlebury is investing in faculty to support the development of new teaching practices.

units.why: 'AI detectors have varied reliability, can demonstrate bias against non-native English speakers' says detectors are unreliable (P39), informs.
units.anchor: AI detectors have varied reliability, can demonstrate bias against non-native English speakers
units.frag_start: At this time, AI detectors have

units.why: 'we recommend that faculty who employ AI detectors do so as supplementary tools ... rather than use these detectors as the sole basis' limits reliance on detectors (P39), should.
units.anchor: we recommend that faculty who employ AI detectors do so as supplementary tools
units.frag_start: At this time, based on evaluations

units.why: 'Stepping up policing around AI use builds an adversarial atmosphere of distrust' (MIT quote) advises against policing AI use; P60 is staff stating they will not police, not general advice, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Stepping up policing around AI use builds an adversarial atmosphere of distrust
units.uncovered_note: Rationale advising instructors against stepping up policing of AI use because it builds distrust and hurts motivation

units.why: 'MIT suggests that faculty have transparent dialogues about AI use' recommends instructors openly discuss expectations with students; nearest is P09 (communicate expectations), should.
units.anchor: faculty have transparent dialogues about AI use, foster intrinsic motivation, and create inclusive classrooms

documents.title: AI Policies / principles page
documents.summary: Short principles page saying AI use must follow existing institutional policies on data classification, IT use and intellectual property, and that policy will evolve. On academic integrity it only says individual instructors may add guidelines.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no position on student AI use; it says 'Individual instructors may provide additional guidelines around AI use in their courses' and points to data, IP and IT policies, so it delegates.

units.why: 'Middlebury College recognizes the profound impact these technologies are having on education, research, and society' opens the policy page with purpose and context (P56), informs.
units.anchor: recognizes the profound impact these technologies are having on education, research, and society
units.frag_start: As we navigate the rapidly evolving

units.why: 'guidance and policy will continue to develop along with the capabilities of the technology' says policy is provisional (P54).
units.anchor: guidance and policy will continue to develop along with the capabilities of the technology
units.frag_start: As this is an emergent technology

units.why: 'AI use at Middlebury must comply with institutional policies' sets the institution-wide principle that AI use falls under existing policies (P56), must.
units.anchor: AI use at Middlebury must comply with institutional policies.
units.frag_start: As with any technology, AI use

units.why: 'AI data should be restricted to public data (Level 1)' protects confidential data in AI tools (P50), should.
units.anchor: AI data should be restricted to public data (Level 1).

units.why: 'please request a consultation with ITS' before using non-public data with a specific AI tool routes use of non-public data through vetting (P50), should.
units.anchor: If you want to use a specific AI tool with non-public Middlebury data

units.why: 'carefully review the AI tool's terms of service for any intellectual property or copyright clauses' concerns licensing and ownership (P52), should.
units.anchor: carefully review the AI tool's terms of service for any intellectual property or copyright clauses

units.why: 'Before using an AI technology make sure you understand how it will treat the content you enter' is IP/content-handling advice (P52 chosen over P50 as the row concerns intellectual property), should.
units.anchor: make sure you understand how it will treat the content you enter

units.why: 'Individual instructors may provide additional guidelines around AI use in their courses' leaves added course rules to instructors (P04), may.
units.anchor: instructors may provide additional guidelines around AI use

notes: Course layer deferred in collect. Policies page repeats the instructor-guidelines sentence under IP and Academic integrity rows; coded once. Dialogue/policing units on the faculty page are quotes of MIT adopted as Middlebury's advice. Sample syllabus statements are addressed to students but are templates, so unit actors reflect the sample text.
